title: When Three Hamzahs come together in One Word.
titleEn: When Three Hamzahs come together in One Word.
description: There are two instances where technically three hamzahs come together in one word; أَأَأْمَنتُم and أَأَأْلِهَتُنَا. Gramatically when two hamzahs come together with the second being sākinah, the second hamzah will be transformed into an alif (madd badal). Thus, we are left with: ءَامَنتُم and ءَأَالِهَتُنَا. The rules for ءَامَنتُم have previously already been covered.

tahqiq_of_both.title: Taḥqīq of both
tahqiq_of_both.description: Both hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) with no changes made to either - ءَأَالِهَتُنَا

tashil_of_second.title: Tashῑl of 2nd
tashil_of_second.description: Tashῑl as described before refers to reciting a hamzah with a blend of the long vowel corresponding to the ḥarakah (short vowel) on it. These qurra will  recite the first of the two hamzahs clearly (taḥqīq) and the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel alif.
